KEY MESSAGE 1...
Areas of dense fog tonight (Sunday night), and possibly again
Monday night. Fog will impact travel conditions.

KEY MESSAGE 1 DESCRIPTION...
Fog is the main concern. Dense fog was present Sunday morning
especially near the coast. With the airmass getting even a bit
moister, think that tonight will be a repeat performance, except
areas further inland will have a better shot at getting the fog.
The best chance of the dense fog is near the Downeast fog, but
can't rule out significant fog further inland too. The fog
should generally dissipate during the day Monday, but fog
appears likely again Monday night. There may be a slightly later
onset to the fog in the evening Monday compared to this (Sunday)
evening, but still think the fog could be locally dense by later
Monday night.

KEY MESSAGE 2...
Chance of showers persists late this (Sunday) afternoon through
Monday afternoon, with possibly thunderstorms in Northern Maine
Monday afternoon.

KEY MESSAGE 2 DESCRIPTION... 
As of 2pm Sunday afternoon, lots of clouds and low-level
moisture, but not much more than drizzle. There are some heavier
showers/storms south of our area that will move north into
especially eastern portions of our area and bring another shot
of showers later this afternoon into the evening. Can't rule out
an embedded storm and some heavier downpours, but nothing
remotely strong for thunderstorms, and no flooding, with a few
places getting another quarter inch of rain or a bit more.
Probably some drying later tonight into Monday morning, but with
a bit of clearing, expect enough instability to showers and
storms to fire off by about midday. Scattered showers/storms are
expected, with the best chance being inland away from the more
stable marine layer. That said, even in the wetter north, only
going with a 40-60 percent chance of showers/storms, best chance
in the western North Woods. Monday won't be a rainout by any
means. Can't rule out a couple of the storms being on the
stronger side with gusty winds, but this is a pretty minimal
threat, and there is some uncertainty how many storms can fire
in the first place.

KEY MESSAGE 3... 
Chance of showers and thunderstorms north of Bangor Tuesday 
and mainly across northern Aroostook Wednesday.

KEY MESSAGE 3 DESCRIPTION...
The axis of an upper level closed low that is gradually
weakening as it passes to the north, then northeast Tuesday-
Wednesday, should bring with it sufficient instability in the
low-mid levels with its associated cold-pool aloft, that is
should produce scattered to potentially numerous showers and
isolated to scattered showers areawide on Tuesday. 

By Tuesday afternoon, low to mid level lapse rates should be 
around 8-8.5C/km, with a few hundred J/kg of CAPE and around 
35-45 kt of bulk shear. This should produce some strong to 
locally severe storms across the region north of Bangor. Wet bulb
zero heights are around 7500-8500 ft away from the coast so the 
greatest risk would be small to possibly marginally severe hail.


On Wednesday,as the upper low weakens and retreats to the 
northeast, the threat will be limited to the North, with low 
level lapse rates around 7.5-8 C/km, around 500-1000 J/kg of 
CAPE and around 20-30 kt of shear. Once again strong to possibly
locally severe storms are possible with mainly isolated storms 
across northern Aroostook. The wetbulb zero height is a little 
higher 8500-9000 J/kg, but still low enough to support hail. With 
the stronger CAPE, the main threat is both strong winds and small 
to marginally severe hail in the strongest convection across the 
North on Wednesday.


KEY MESSAGE 4... 
Thunderstorms are possible Friday afternoon and evening, some
of which may be locally strong side with gusty winds and small 
hail.

KEY MESSAGE 4 DESCRIPTION... 
A cold front crosses the area Friday afternoon and evening on 
the leading edge of a full latitude trough pushing into the 
region, with the added support of a northern stream shortwave 
pushing through the trough around that time. With the potential 
for 500-1500 J/kg of CAPE and 25-35KT of bulk shear, there is a
risk of some locally strong thunderstorms ahead of the front, 
with the main threat strong gusty winds.
